chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah Jabala al-Kinani, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) met me while I was dangling a fish in my hand, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Throw it away! I dislike for the eminent man that he should carry the humble thing by himself.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'You are a people whose enemies are many; the creation has been hostile to you, O group of Shiah, the creation has been hostile to you. Therefore, adorn yourselves to them with what you are able to do.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of 'adorn yourselves' (fatazayyanu) in Shia social etiquette?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) uses the physical act of discarding a fish to illustrate the principle of dignified conduct, advising that prominent figures should not burden themselves with humble tasks alone. He expands this into a broader socio-political strategy for the Shia community, urging them to 'adorn' themselves with good manners and appearance (tazayyun) to win over their numerous enemies and mitigate hostility in a time of political vulnerability.

en.hubeali: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Jabala Al Kinany who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> met me and I was dangling a fish in my hand, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Throw it away! I<sup>asws</sup> dislike for the eminent man that he should be carrying the abject thing by himself’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The group of your enemies are numerous. The people are your enemies, O group of Shiah, people hold grudges against you. Therefore adorn yourselves to them with your ability over it’.
en.sarwar: 12. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah al-Kinaniy who has said the following:

“Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, welcomed me and I was hanging a fish in my hand. He (the Imam) said, ‘Throw it away; I dislike that a noble and high ranking man himself carry something unimportant.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You are a people who have a large number of enemies. People are your enemies, O Shi ‘ah, because you have become their enemies, therefore, you must beautify yourselves before them to whatever degree you can.’”
